newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland Fed median CPI up 0.3 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland Fed median CPI up 0.3 pct in January.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland said its measure of the median Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.3 percent in January after a 0.2 percent increase the month before.
On an annualized basis, the median CPI grew at a 3.1 percent rate, the Cleveland Fed said.
Median CPI is a core measure of inflation calculated by the Cleveland Fed based on the Bureau of Labor Statistics's monthly CPI data.
Unlike the core CPI, which specifically excludes food and energy prices, the median CPI excludes any item whose price diverges markedly from the performance of most components in the CPI.
"Over the last 12 months, the median CPI advanced 2.8 percent, the CPI rose 3.0 percent and the CPI less food energy climbed 2.5 percent," the regional Fed bank said.
